title: Part 2.I — Scene (Philosophic Schools)

outline.label: The Featuring of the Terms — programmatic statement: seven philosophic idioms generated by the pentad (+ nominalism, rationalism); each school 'features' one pentad term with the others slighted or placed in its perspective.
Scene in General — Baldwin + Encyclopaedia Britannica + Paulsen definitions of materialism; the narrowing of scenic circumference to motion; Santayana epigraph on the dead atom.

Hobbes — mechanistic materialism; Leviathan as 'art whereby God hath made and governs the world'; sense as caused by external body, imagination as 'decaying sense', reason as motion of addition/subtraction, will as 'last appetite in deliberating'; reduction of will to scene-mechanically-determined motion; tactical re-emergence of 'action' under pressure of the moral category.

Spinoza — Deus sive Natura as 'action equals motion'; causa sui (active+passive); natura naturans / natura naturata as primus inter pares pair; conatus in suo esse perseverandi as scenically-derived agent-equivalent; geometrical method as scenic/contextual; 'all determination is negation'; scenic circumference covers act, agent, agency, purpose.

Alignment of Terms in Spinoza — thought/extension Cartesian pair set aside in favor of the action/passion pair; full Active/Passive ledger (self-caused vs externally caused, infinite vs finite, natura naturans vs natura naturata, freedom vs bondage, intrinsic vs extrinsic, adequate vs inadequate ideas, etc.); intellectual love of God; three kinds of knowledge (imagination/reason/intuition); intuition derived from Reason, hence still scenic.

Darwin — 'Conditions of Existence' as the higher law subsuming Unity of Type; natural selection as scenic; ambiguities of 'adaptation', 'competition', 'survival of the fittest' as quasi-action words; Mivart counter (internal force) and Darwin's bare-minimum concession to agent; biology as 'agent-minus'; the Mendelian 'idealoid' contrast; the Janus function of 'variability' standing where scene overlaps agent; whole organism treated as environment for its own parts.

The Two Great Hellenistic Materialisms — Epicurus/Lucretius (atomic-swerve; the clinamen / parenklisis as 'pre-agentification of scene'; chance combination as proto-Darwinian) vs. Stoicism (pronoia/Providence as purposive scene; cosmic Reason; Marcus Aurelius's moral utilitarianism as bridge from Providence to pragmatism).

Rhetorical and Symbolic Levels — six numbered observations on how grammatical scene-featuring impinges on rhetoric/symbolic: (1) Lucretius's De Rerum Natura cross-purposes (Venus-invocation vs plague-ending); (2) materialist debunking as transformation of ghosts into corpses (childhood→adult pattern); (3) Lucretius's Poeni/Poenae pun and the mother-Earth matrix; (4) Stoic outbursts against the flesh as 'transcendence of offal'; (5) Epictetus vs Marcus Aurelius — manumitted slave vs emperor, different tones of Stoic progress (prokopē); (6) Reichian reading of Aurelius's sex-repression as political dispiriting; closing flag that Marx and Santayana (two further materialisms) are deferred until after Agent.

concepts.label: Scene (pentad term)
concepts.gloss: The pentad term answering 'where/in what situation?' — the background of the act, the situation in which the act occurs. Materialism's featured term.

concepts.label: Featuring of a term
concepts.gloss: Burke's diagnostic move: each philosophic school selects one of the five terms as Ausgangspunkt (generating principle) and develops a vocabulary suited to give that term full expression, with the other four slighted or placed in its perspective.

concepts.label: Materialism
concepts.gloss: The philosophic terminology corresponding to the featuring of scene; reduces facts of the universe to body/matter in motion; narrows scenic circumference so that action is reduced to motion.

concepts.label: Circumference of scene
concepts.gloss: The scope or boundary one draws around the scenic ground of an act; materialism narrows the circumference so as to exclude personal/spiritual causes.

concepts.label: Reduction of action to motion
concepts.gloss: The defining materialist move: the vocabulary of action is replaced by the vocabulary of motion; sense, imagination, will, passion all redescribed as motions of/in the body.

concepts.label: Pre-agentification of scene
concepts.gloss: Burke's term for the way Hellenistic materialisms (esp. Epicureanism and Stoicism) endow the scene with properties of agent (atomic swerve; cosmic Reason) so that imputed motives can be deduced from the quality of the ground.

concepts.label: Agentification
concepts.gloss: The translation of scenic terms into agentic terms (or vice versa); Burke's general label for one-term migrations among the pentad members.

concepts.label: Hobbesian mechanism
concepts.gloss: Hobbes's reductive program: imagination as 'decaying sense', reason as addition/subtraction of names, will as 'last appetite in deliberating', passions as appetite/aversion (hormē/aphormē); man as automaton; State as gigantic man.

concepts.label: Deus sive Natura
concepts.gloss: Spinoza's pantheist equation God=Nature; Burke reads it as 'action equals motion'; the scenic word God serves as ground/medium of the scene-act ratio in which action becomes possible.

concepts.label: Natura naturans / natura naturata
concepts.gloss: Spinoza's distinction between 'naturing nature' (active) and 'natured nature' (passive); a primus-inter-pares pair where, despite formal equality, the active term is foremost — God as active scene.

concepts.label: Conatus in suo esse perseverandi
concepts.gloss: Spinoza's endeavor of each being to persevere in its being; Burke reads it as a scenically-derived agent-equivalent — an internal motivational locus generated within the larger scenic framework of Substance.

concepts.label: All determination is negation
concepts.gloss: Spinoza's formula; Burke reads it as evidence that Spinoza's geometry is essentially scenic/contextual — each finite thing is determined by the boundaries other things impose on it.

concepts.label: Intellectual love of God (amor Dei intellectualis)
concepts.gloss: Spinoza's summum bonum; reading particulars sub specie aeternitatis in their total context; Burke flags this as still scenic despite its apparent move toward idealism.

concepts.label: Three kinds of knowledge
concepts.gloss: Spinoza's hierarchy: imagination/opinion (inadequate), Reason (ratio), and intuition (scientia intuitiva); Burke notes intuition is derived from Reason, hence still scenic — opposite of the Bergsonian intuition that transcends reason.

concepts.label: Conditions of Existence (Darwin)
concepts.gloss: Darwin's higher law subsuming Unity of Type; Burke reads it as a near-perfect materialist reduction-to-scene, but flags the 'agent-minus' pressure exerted by the language of selection/competition/adaptation.

concepts.label: Variability (Darwin)
concepts.gloss: Burke's Janus-faced Darwinian key term: stands at the point where scene overlaps agent; allows two meanings (cause ab extra vs. internal principle of motion). Functionally analogous to the Epicurean clinamen.

concepts.label: Agent-minus (organism)
concepts.gloss: Burke's improvised category for the biologist's 'organism': a partial agent, classed under agent only insofar as its behavior has to be accounted for by some internal principle of self-movement; reflects same scenic reduction as the bubble rising to the surface.

concepts.label: Clinamen / parenklisis (atomic swerve)
concepts.gloss: Lucretius's small swerve of atoms; Burke reads it as a scenic derivation for human freedom — a 'seed' of action lodged in pure motion, opening toward agent and act from within the materialist vocabulary.

concepts.label: Pronoia (Stoic Providence)
concepts.gloss: Stoic equation of Nature with Providence/Reason/Will-of-God; introduces purposive scene; the agency-purpose ratio reappears inside materialism, building a bridge from Providence to pragmatism.

concepts.label: Prokopē (progress)
concepts.gloss: Stoic concept of moral progress / spiritual emancipation; Burke contrasts Epictetus's slave-to-freedom prokopē with Aurelius's emperor-disciplining-the-self prokopē — same word, two scenic situations.

concepts.label: Rhetorical and Symbolic Levels
concepts.gloss: Burke's frame for moving from purely Grammatical scene-featuring to the Rhetorical (persuasion-effects) and Symbolic (latent imagery/guilt patterns) registers of the same philosophy; demonstrated via six observations on Lucretius/Aurelius/Epictetus.

concepts.label: Transcendence of offal
concepts.gloss: Burke's diagnostic phrase for Stoic sudden outbursts against the body — moments when the philosophy's 'transubstantiation of the excremental' (declaring the world divine in all its aspects) collapses into mere repugnance at offal.

concepts.label: Scene-act ratio (materialist construal)
concepts.gloss: The materialist version of the scene-act ratio: the act follows mechanically from the scene; will is what the scenic balance of appetites tips toward; freedom is consent to necessity (Spinoza) or non-impedance of motion (Hobbes).

concepts.label: Scene-agent ratio (materialist construal)
concepts.gloss: The materialist version of scene-agent ratio: agent traits are derivable from scenic ground (Hobbesian sovereignty as artificial soul; Darwinian variability as scenically-induced; Spinozistic conatus as ground-derived endeavor).

concepts.label: Ausgangspunkt
concepts.gloss: Burke's term (German, 'point of departure') for the pentad-term a philosophy takes as its generating principle; each school's Ausgangspunkt generates a set of problems and a derived vocabulary.

positions.claim: Materialism is the philosophic terminology that features Scene as the locus of motive.
positions.support: Burke's enumerated correspondences (book p.128); Baldwin/Britannica/Paulsen definitions cited (book p.131); Hobbes/Spinoza/Darwin/Epicureanism/Stoicism all developed under this header.

positions.claim: Featuring Scene narrows the circumference of motivation by replacing the vocabulary of action with the vocabulary of motion.
positions.support: Burke's explicit Britannica gloss + Santayana epigraph 'the atom must be quite dead' (book pp.131-132); Hobbes's reduction of sense/imagination/will/passion to motion (book pp.133-136).

positions.claim: Hobbes's materialism contains a tactical re-emergence of action (will, voluntary act) under the pressure of the moral category and the heritage of dramatistic theology, which materialism's program tries to transform into the mechanical but cannot wholly suppress.
positions.support: Burke's commentary book pp.136-137; Hobbes speaking of 'action' where his vocabulary calls for 'motion'; Hobbes treating moral/ethical matter while pledged to mechanism.

positions.claim: Spinoza occupies a watershed position more ambiguously placed than Hobbes — his action/motion equation (Deus sive Natura) lets him be claimed by either materialism (stress Nature) or pantheism (stress God); the action side is in fact stressed, distinguishing him from Hobbes.
positions.support: Burke book pp.137-141; the active/passive ledger of natura naturans / natura naturata; Spinoza's primus-inter-pares strategy in equating the two; reading the action term as foremost.

positions.claim: The conatus performs Spinoza's agent-function but is scenically derived: Spinoza's terminology generates an internal motivational locus by limited application of the same God/Nature/Substance principles that constitute the scenic whole.
positions.support: Burke book pp.144-145 on conatus as ground-derived agent-equivalent; the modes as 'parts of the whole'; intrinsic essence still scenically derived.

positions.claim: Spinoza's geometrical method is dramatistically scenic, not formally-axiomatic: it presents the world as a structure of contextual terminations ('all determination is negation') rather than as a system of motion-laws.
positions.support: Burke book pp.143-144; geometry as more than borrowed Euclidean device; finite things as negations within total positive Context (God).

positions.claim: Darwin is materialist in conscious intention (Conditions of Existence as higher law) but the dynastic/familial pattern of his biological subject matter exerts a quasi-idealistic pressure toward agent — visible in his concessions to Mivart, in 'variability' as a Janus term, and in the heraldic plan-of-creation rhetoric.
positions.support: Burke book pp.153-158; the Mivart correspondence; variability standing at scene/agent overlap; biology as 'agent-minus'.

positions.claim: The two Hellenistic materialisms both perform a 'pre-agentification of scene' but by opposite devices: Epicureanism by lodging an internal swerve (clinamen) in the atom, Stoicism by saturating the cosmic scene with Providence/Reason/purpose.
positions.support: Burke book pp.159-161; the clinamen as scenic seed of freedom; pronoia as purposive scene; agency-purpose ratio reappearing inside the materialist vocabulary.

positions.claim: Stoicism builds a bridge 'from Providence to pragmatism' through its purposive-scenic concept of Nature-as-divine-plan, anticipating the agency-purpose ratio's later pragmatist deployment.
positions.support: Burke book p.161; Marcus Aurelius's moral utilitarianism; everything brought about for a use; incipient pragmatism but pre-modern-technology.

positions.claim: Rhetorical and Symbolic levels of a scene-featuring philosophy can reveal latent dramatic content the grammatical level represses — Lucretius's plague-ending and Mother-Venus/Mother-Earth matrix, Aurelius's sudden hatreds-of-the-flesh, Epictetus's freed-slave prokopē are diagnostic windows.
positions.support: Burke's six numbered observations book pp.161-169; Lucretius De Rerum Natura cross-purposes; Stoic 'transcendence of offal'; Reichian reading of Aurelius.

positions.claim: Scene-featuring under materialism is diagnosed by which level of analysis a philosophy takes as motive-locus, not by surface vocabulary — agency-talk and agent-talk borrowed by other schools can look materialist (e.g. 'the literary situation') without being so.
positions.support: Burke book pp.129-130; the 'situation' synonymy and the misappropriation by idealistic/agency-stressed literary criticism.

positions.claim: Materialism's symmetry is never perfect: in each canonical materialist (Hobbes, Spinoza, Darwin, Lucretius, Aurelius) the suppressed pentad terms — especially act, agent, purpose — re-enter the vocabulary at strategic points, leaving traces Burke calls the 'pressure of the other terms'.
positions.support: Burke's recurring formula across all five philosophers (book pp.135, 145, 154-155, 160, 161); the pentad's 'continual press for consideration' (book p.130).

philosophers_cited.name: Hobbes (Thomas)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Frames Hobbes as the most thorough exemplar of vocabulary systematically built on 'extension'; treats Leviathan as machine-metaphor literalized; reads sense, imagination, will, passion as reductions of action to motion; flags the 'tactical' re-emergence of action under moral pressure as evidence the pentad's other terms cannot be fully suppressed.

philosophers_cited.name: Spinoza (Baruch)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Treats Spinoza as the chapter's central interlocutor; reads Deus sive Natura as the watershed action=motion equation; constructs an Active/Passive ledger out of his terms; reads conatus as scenically-derived agent-equivalent; reads geometry as dramatistically contextual; reads intuition as derived-from-Reason (still scenic); diagnoses Spinozism as scene-featuring whose ethical stress lets it function as a bridge from theological-to-naturalistic and from naturalistic-to-idealistic vocabularies.

philosophers_cited.name: Darwin (Charles)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Reads Conditions of Existence as materialist higher law; tracks the pressure of agent in adaptation/competition/survival rhetoric; isolates 'variability' as a Janus term where scene overlaps agent; introduces 'agent-minus' (organism) as Grammatical equivalent; contrasts Darwinian materialist breeding-by-conditions with Mendelian 'idealoid' breeding-by-internal-laws.

philosophers_cited.name: Lucretius
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Reads atomic swerve (clinamen / parenklisis) as 'pre-agentification of scene' — an internal seed of action lodged in pure motion; tracks the rhetorical/symbolic cross-purposes of De Rerum Natura (Venus-invocation vs plague-ending; Mother-Venus/Mother-Earth matrix; the Poeni/Poenae pun) as evidence of a goaded materialism whose poetic and philosophic identities clash.

philosophers_cited.name: Epicurus / Epicureanism
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Reads Epicurean cosmology as scenic featuring with the swerve performing the same agent-bridge function the variability concept performs for Darwin; contrasts Epicurean aloofness/individualism (post-polis breakdown) with Stoic civic universalism; reads 'imagine a whole city of Epicureans!' as marking the social-political limits of Epicurean withdrawal.

philosophers_cited.name: Stoicism / Marcus Aurelius / Epictetus
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Reads Stoicism as scene-featuring under the sign of pronoia/Providence — purposive scene that builds a bridge 'from Providence to pragmatism'; distinguishes Epictetus (manumitted slave; prokopē as ladder from spiritual slavery to freedom) from Marcus Aurelius (emperor; voluntary self-subjection; Stoic outbursts against the flesh as 'transcendence of offal'); reads the Aurelian diary as Reichian sex-repression-as-political-dispiriting test case.

philosophers_cited.name: Santayana (George)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Cited via Aspects of Scientific Rationalism in the Nineteenth Century as the chapter's epigraph on the 'dead atom' — materialism's narrowing of scenic circumference; named in the final paragraph as one of two further materialisms (with Marx) postponed until after Agent because both are strongly affected by German transcendentalism.

philosophers_cited.name: Mivart (St George)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Cited via Darwin's reply to him in Origin of Species; Mivart's posited 'internal force or tendency' is the agentic counter-claim Darwin minimally concedes; Burke reads the concession as the place where the pressure of agent is visible inside Darwinian materialism.

philosophers_cited.name: Leibniz (Gottfried)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Cited tangentially: principe de convenance and Leibniz's 'no substance without action, no body without motion' formula as a counterpart move within idealism that resolves the necessity/purpose tension Spinoza encounters.

philosophers_cited.name: Kant (Immanuel)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Cited tangentially: Kant's God/freedom/immortality triad anchors morality (=action) and signals where materialism's scenic vocabulary will eventually be replaced by idealism's agentic vocabulary (treated in GM-05).

philosophers_cited.name: Augustine (Saint)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Cited via Lovejoy's Great Chain of Being on Augustine locating the point of origin in God's will (= absolutely unmotivated act) as the foil against which Spinoza's pantheistic merger of God/Nature in 'necessary' relation is set.

philosophers_cited.name: Bergson (Henri)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Cited as the contrast figure for Spinoza's intuition: Bergsonian intuition transcends and is hostile to reason, whereas Spinozistic intuition is derived from reason and continuous with it — both labeled 'intuition' but scenically opposed.

philosophers_cited.name: Coleridge (Samuel Taylor)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Tangential reference (chapter contains only minor passing allusions; Coleridge is GM-08 material).

philosophers_cited.name: Shakespeare (William)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Cited via Coriolanus's belly-and-members parable as a literary-figurative use of the body-politic analogy contrasted with Hobbes's literal mechanistic use of the same figure.

philosophers_cited.name: Reich (Wilhelm)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Cited 'only by hearsay' (Burke disclaims direct study) but used to read Marcus Aurelius's sexual repression as a political-dispiriting device — a Symbolic-level diagnosis applied to a scene-featuring philosophy.

philosophers_cited.name: Engels / Marx
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Marx cited as the 'powerfully public' modern materialism contrasted with Santayana's 'serenely private' modern materialism; both postponed because German-transcendentalist-affected. Engels mentioned for the Reich-related sexuality counter-example.

philosophers_cited.name: Democritus
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Acknowledged as the ancestor materialist surviving only in fragments; Hobbes presented as the 'most thorough and picturesque' exemplar in his place.

philosophers_cited.name: Empson (William)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Cited for the studies-of-ambiguity warrant by which Burke reads Lucretius's Poeni/Poenae ablative ambiguity as semantically active (Carthaginians and goddesses of Vengeance both audible).

philosophers_cited.name: Aurelius (Marcus)
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Treated as the chapter's exemplar Stoic emperor whose Meditations Burke reads dramatistically — diary written 'in private' but addressed to multiple sub-personalities; secret addressee a 'philosophy-minded subject' the emperor persuades to remain content with material deprivation; whole structure read as scenic ground-of-political-stability.

philosophers_cited.name: Epictetus
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Treated as the slave-Stoic counterpart to Aurelius; freedom located in inner powers and 'impressions' rather than property; prokopē as spiritual ascent from below; freedman's progress essentially different from modern pragmatist 'progress'.

philosophers_cited.name: Cicero / Lovejoy / Arnold (Matthew) / Lucretius's editor / Newton / Schelling
philosophers_cited.burke_move: Various tangential citations: Cicero as the contemporary Roman context of Lucretius; Lovejoy as source for Augustine; Arnold's commentary on Aurelius's enfeeblement; Newton for celestial mechanics; Schelling for subject-object third-term comparison to Spinoza's primus-inter-pares strategy.

scene_term_operationalization.operational_definition: Scene is the pentad term answering the question 'where and in what situation was the act done?'. It names the background, setting, situation, or containing environment that frames an act and within which an agent moves. As containing-principle for action, scene fixes the circumference within which motive may be located; it carries the implicit claim that the act/agent it surrounds can be in part derived from it.
scene_term_operationalization.question_answered: Where (and in what situation, ground, environment, condition) was the act done?
paradigm_examples_from_burke: Hobbesian external body causing sense and imagination (book p.133)
Spinozistic God-Nature as scenic substance from which finite modes are derived (book pp.137-138)
Darwinian 'Conditions of Existence' as higher law (book p.153)
Lucretian atomic void within which atoms fall, swerve, collide (book pp.159-160)
The literary 'situation' (a borrowed scenic term redeployed by other schools, book p.129)
scene_term_operationalization.school_burke_diagnosis: Materialism is the philosophic terminology corresponding to the featuring of scene. It narrows the scenic circumference such that action is reduced to motion and personal/spiritual causes are excluded; the originating ground of motive is environmental, material, and deterministic. All canonical materialists develop an Ausgangspunkt-vocabulary of body-and-motion and either suppress, reduce, or scenically derive the other four pentad terms (Hobbes: will-as-last-appetite; Spinoza: conatus-from-Substance; Darwin: organism-as-agent-minus; Lucretius: clinamen-as-scenic-freedom; Stoicism: purpose-as-providential-scene).
decision_rules_for_scene_attribution: If a motive-statement explains an act primarily by appeal to environmental conditions, situation, ground, or surrounding material/social/historical context, classify the explanation as scene-featuring.

If a putative agent (e.g. Darwinian organism, Spinozistic conatus) is described as derived from or reducible to the larger ground (Substance, Conditions of Existence, atomic void), reclassify as scene-featuring-with-agent-minus.

If the vocabulary of action is systematically replaced by the vocabulary of motion (motion of body, of nerves, of atoms), the discourse is scene-featuring even when surface terms ('will', 'action') survive (Hobbes test).

If 'situation' is used in a sense that means 'motives peculiar to a writer's medium' or 'motives peculiar to men as men', it is NOT scene-featuring — the term has been borrowed by an agency-featuring or agent-featuring school (Burke book pp.129-130).

If a putative scenic ground is endowed with purposive/rational properties (Stoic pronoia) or with internal-tendency-to-deviate (Epicurean clinamen), classify as scene-featuring-with-pre-agentification.
Resolve scene/agent ambiguity by tracing where the philosophy's Ausgangspunkt lies — whether terms for ground are generative of terms for self-movement or vice versa.
scene_term_operationalization.calleja_pim_mapping_rationale: Scene maps most strongly to Calleja's Spatial dimension because both name the bounded, subjectively-constituted environment within which involvement is constituted (game-world, room, social context). Scene maps secondarily to Kinesthetic because the body-in-space subdimension of player involvement is itself a scene-agent ratio at the player's micro-temporal phase — the controller-handling, perceptual-orienting body inhabits and is partly constituted by the spatial scene.
scene_term_operationalization.uexkull_mapping_rationale: STRONGEST anticipated cross-pipeline mapping. Burke's containing-Scene and Uexküll's Umwelt converge structurally on the same insight: motive-locus is a bounded, subjectively-constituted environment that delivers perceptual cues (Merkwelt / scene-as-given) and absorbs effector outputs (Wirkwelt / scene-as-acted-upon). Burke 1945 cannot exegetically cite Uexküll (0 hits per Phase 0 cite-check; English translation 1957/2010), so the bridge is anticipatory-projection (dissertation); parallel-discovery, not influence.
scene_term_operationalization.ontological_grounding_rationale: Scene's grammatical function as containing-principle for action structurally parallels Heidegger's In-der-Welt-sein (being-in-the-world) and Befindlichkeit (state-of-mind/situatedness/attunement) as the existential structure within which Dasein discloses an act. Anticipatory only — Burke 1945 contains 0 Heidegger hits per Phase 0; the Macquarrie-Robinson translation of Sein und Zeit is 1962. Provenance must be marked anticipatory-projection (dissertation) via BCAP and Being and Time corpus indices.
scene_term_operationalization.dissertation_game_analytic_target: Game-world (geometry, level design, environmental affordances) + room (the player's physical room as outer Scene) + social context (multiplayer scene, streaming scene, viewer-audience scene); the spatial Calleja-PIM macro-phase + outer-scene/inner-scene distinction of GM-03 (book pp.77-85) imported as the dissertation's macro-to-micro scenic-circumference apparatus.
scene_term_operationalization.forward_reference_to_rhetoric_of_motives: When the Rhetoric pipeline is built, Scene's operationalization will need an Attitude modifier: the affective/dispositional coloring with which an agent stands within a scene. Calleja's Affective dimension maps to Attitude rather than Scene proper; dissertation Manual Section A should keep this Attitude-modifier slot open.

philosophic_school_mapping.burke_diagnostic: The school whose vocabulary is generated by treating Scene as the Ausgangspunkt and whose other pentad terms are reduced, slighted, or scenically derived.

philosopher_table.burke_exegetical_move: Reads Hobbes as the most thorough exemplar of vocabulary systematically built on extension; the Leviathan's machine-metaphor literalized; sense, imagination, will, passion all redescribed as motion; will reduced to 'last appetite in deliberating'; action re-emerges tactically under the pressure of the moral category and the inherited dramatistic-theological vocabulary.
philosopher_table.scenic_signature: Mechanism — body, motion, extension as Ausgangspunkt; State as gigantic man as scenic-into-social projection.
philosopher_table.pressure_of_other_terms: Act re-emerges under moral pressure (book pp.136-137); Agent re-emerges as the artificial person/sovereign of Leviathan; Burke flags both as proof that pentad's suppressed terms cannot be wholly extinguished.

philosopher_table.burke_exegetical_move: Treats Spinoza as the chapter's central interlocutor at the watershed moment; reads Deus sive Natura as action=motion equation with the action-side ultimately foremost (primus inter pares); constructs an Active/Passive ledger from his terms; reads conatus as scenically-derived agent-equivalent; reads geometry as dramatistically contextual (all determination is negation); reads intuition as derived-from-Reason hence still scenic; diagnoses Spinozism as scene-featuring whose ethical stress functions as a bridge from theological to naturalistic and from naturalistic to idealistic vocabularies.
philosopher_table.scenic_signature: Pantheism — God=Nature as scenic Substance; natura naturans / natura naturata as active/passive partition of the same scenic whole; modes as parts of Substance.
philosopher_table.pressure_of_other_terms: Agent (conatus) ground-derived; Act (intellectual love of God) emerging at idealism-edge; Purpose 'retreats behind rational necessity' but is not eliminated; the Spinozist alignment-of-terms preserves all five pentad members in active/passive form.

philosopher_table.burke_exegetical_move: Reads Conditions of Existence as materialist higher law subsuming Unity of Type; tracks the agentic-pressure exerted by adaptation/competition/survival-of-the-fittest rhetoric; isolates variability as the Janus term where scene overlaps agent; introduces 'agent-minus' as the Grammatical category for biological organism; contrasts Darwinian breeding-by-external-conditions with Mendelian 'idealoid' breeding-by-internal-laws.
philosopher_table.scenic_signature: Evolutionary materialism — environment as differential selector; familial/dynastic structure of organic descent as quasi-scene.
philosopher_table.pressure_of_other_terms: Agent re-emerges in the Mivart concession ('tendency to ordinary variability'); Purpose re-emerges where Darwin slips into language of utility/contrivance (the flower's color-for-insect-attraction); the Mendelian counterpart (Burke flags as 'quasi-idealistic biology') points toward Agent-featuring.

philosopher_table.burke_exegetical_move: Reads the atomic clinamen as 'pre-agentification of scene' — an internal swerve lodged in pure motion that gives a scenic derivation for human freedom; tracks the rhetorical/symbolic cross-purposes of De Rerum Natura (Venus-invocation vs plague-ending; Mother-Venus/Mother-Earth/human-mother matrix; Poeni/Poenae ablative pun); reads the work as a goaded materialism in which philosophic identity and poetic identity clash, leaving traces of unresolved guilt.
philosopher_table.scenic_signature: Atomism — void + atoms + swerve as scenic ground; chance combination as proto-evolutionary motor; ethical implication: free from fear of gods because gods are scenically-absent.
philosopher_table.pressure_of_other_terms: Act re-emerges via the swerve's role as freedom-derivation; Agent re-emerges via the maternal-matrix and the goaded-by-something-author position; Purpose suppressed but the plague-ending suggests a Symbolic-level purpose-shadow.

philosopher_table.burke_exegetical_move: Reads Epicurean cosmology as scenic-featuring with the swerve performing the same agent-bridge that variability performs for Darwin; contrasts Epicurean post-polis individualism / aloofness with Stoic civic universalism; reads the gods'-aloofness-from-worldly-things as both Epicurean self-ideal and source of unconscience-twinge in civic life.
philosopher_table.scenic_signature: Atomic-and-void scene with built-in chance-deviation; pleasure/aloofness as ethical implication of the same scene.
philosopher_table.pressure_of_other_terms: Agent (the Epicurean sage as ataraxic withdrawer) emerges as scene-conditioned; Purpose (eudaimonia as living-up-to-divine-aloofness) survives as ethical telos but is suppressed in cosmology proper.

philosopher_table.burke_exegetical_move: Reads Stoicism as scene-featuring under the sign of pronoia/Providence — a purposive cosmic scene equating Nature with Providence/Reason/Will-of-God; builds the bridge from Providence to pragmatism; distinguishes Epictetus (manumitted slave; prokopē-from-below) from Marcus Aurelius (emperor; voluntary self-subjection; sudden hatreds of the flesh as 'transcendence of offal'); deploys Reich heuristically to read Aurelian sex-repression as political-dispiriting.
philosopher_table.scenic_signature: Cosmos-as-providential-plan; Nature=Reason=God; ethical implication of moral utilitarianism, civic universalism, expanded citizenship.
philosopher_table.pressure_of_other_terms: Purpose is so heavily present (pronoia) that the school risks crossing into mysticism; Agency emerges as pragmatist-bridge; Act re-emerges in the dialectical voice (especially Stoicism's earlier dialecticians) and in the diary's plural-sub-personality structure (Aurelius); Agent re-emerges as the Stoic philosophy-minded subject the diary addresses.

tensions.label: Symmetry break: action re-emerges where motion ought to suffice (Hobbes / Spinoza)
tensions.description: Both Hobbes and Spinoza pledge the reduction of action to motion but find action re-emerging at the strategic moment of ethical/moral discussion. Burke names this the 'partial break in symmetry' and reads it as evidence of the pentad's continual press for consideration — the suppressed terms force their way back into the vocabulary under categorical pressure.
tensions.implication: Materialism cannot eliminate Act; it can only redescribe it. Dissertation deployment: a game-design framework that programmatically reduces player-motive to environmental affordance will encounter the same symmetry break under ethical pressure (loot-box debates, dark-pattern critiques).

tensions.label: Pre-agentification of scene (Hellenistic materialisms)
tensions.description: Both Epicureanism (clinamen) and Stoicism (pronoia) endow the scenic ground with properties of an agent — internal swerve in the first case, cosmic Reason in the second. The result is that materialism's scenic Ausgangspunkt absorbs agentic properties rather than eliminating them, generating bridges to either freedom-as-spontaneity (Epicurean) or freedom-as-rational-necessity (Stoic).
tensions.implication: Scene can be 'thickened' with agency by endowing it with internal devices (swerve, providence). Dissertation deployment: game-world AI, procedural generation, and emergent narrative systems all function as pre-agentified scene — the level itself behaves quasi-agentically without being a discrete agent.

tensions.label: Scenic vs. idealistic Spinozism
tensions.description: Spinoza's intellectual love of God + the eternity of mind + the apparent Platonist transcendence at the close of Ethics could be read as movements toward idealism; Burke insists they are still scenic because particulars are always understood in their total context. Yet Burke concedes the closing of the Ethics 'clearly moves us in the direction of idealism' — leaving Spinoza at a permanently watershed position.
tensions.implication: A philosophy can be scene-featuring AND host genuine agentic/idealistic moments without ceasing to be scene-featuring; the diagnostic is the Ausgangspunkt and the generative direction, not the inventory of moments. Dissertation deployment: a game studies theory can feature one pentad term while productively hosting others.

tensions.label: Variability as Janus term (Darwin)
tensions.description: Darwin's 'variability' allows two meanings: cause-from-without (scenic) and internal-principle-of-motion (agentic). Burke calls this a Janus function: the term pliantly stands at the point where scene overlaps agent and lets Darwin use it for both kinds of explanation. The ambiguity is a strategic resource rather than a defect.
tensions.implication: Some pentad-overlap terms are productively ambiguous rather than ill-defined. Dissertation deployment: terms like 'engagement', 'flow', 'agency' in game studies discourse function as Janus terms between Scene-PIM and Agency-PIM.

tensions.label: Grammatical vs Rhetorical/Symbolic levels diverge
tensions.description: A scene-featuring philosophy at the Grammatical level may carry counter-current Rhetorical and Symbolic content: Lucretius's plague-ending and mother-matrix; Aurelius's sudden hatreds of the body; Epictetus's prokopē-from-slavery; the Reichian reading of imperial sex-repression. The Symbolic-plane content can run against the philosophy's stated Grammatical commitment.
tensions.implication: Operationalizing pentad-diagnosis must distinguish a discourse's Grammatical-level claim from its Rhetorical/Symbolic-level traces. Dissertation deployment: a game's stated design philosophy and the player-experiences/community-discourse it generates can diverge along Grammatical/Rhetorical/Symbolic lines.
